subject: Exec approval: Optimize Guardrails gating override policy (Enterprise tiers)
attachments: Optimize Guardrails - Override policy options v2 (Google Doc link)
body:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Exec approval: Optimize Guardrails gating override policy (Enterprise tiers)

Priya — requesting a decision today/tomorrow so we can finalize PM-844 / ENG-3920.

Question: Do we allow an “override gating” path for Enterprise tiers (Dedicated + Private) when Optimize applies a cost-saving config change (quant profile, batching/caching, routing tweak) and the guardrails gate fails (or times out)?

Context:
- We’ve had at least one enterprise prospect (Acme Fintech) explicitly ask for a path to proceed in an emergency (“we accept risk, but need paper trail”).
- Security/compliance folks are okay with an override only if audit logs are unambiguous + exportable.
- Platform preference is “no override” for self-serve tiers; question is whether we also keep that strictness for enterprise.

Decision options (short):
A) No override anywhere (hard block on fail/timeout). Strongest quality posture, but can block high-priority customers during runner outages / false positives.
B) Override allowed only for Enterprise (Dedicated/Private) + only for specific failure modes (runner unavailable/timeout), not for “true fail”.
C) Override allowed for Enterprise for both fail + timeout, but requires additional controls (justification, approval, TTL, rerun eval).

If we allow override, we need clarity on:
- Who can do it (roles) and whether we require a second approver.
- Required audit fields + retention.
- Whether override is permitted for quantization changes (highest risk).

Attachment stubs:
- Optimize Guardrails - Override policy options v2 (Google Doc link)
- OptimizeConfigChange audit event fields - draft.csv

Thanks,
Ava

—
Ava Chen
Security & Compliance (GTM)
Redwood Inference



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Optimize Guardrails gating override policy (Enterprise tiers)

+1 on needing an enterprise path.

Two product notes:
1) “No override anywhere” is clean, but we’ll lose momentum in pilots if we can’t unblock a customer due to runner timeouts/flaky evals. We’ve already seen timeouts in staging when backlog spikes.
2) We should treat quantization differently. If override exists, it should be harder for quant changes vs batching/caching tweaks.

My preference:
- Enterprise only (Dedicated/Private), feature-flagged.
- Allow override for timeouts/runner unavailable by default.
- Allow override for “fail” only with explicit approval (and ideally a second approver) + mandatory follow-up rerun.

Happy to align on the minimum bar from auditing.

Aditya



From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Optimize Guardrails gating override policy (Enterprise tiers)

Implementation constraints / what’s realistic:

- We can implement an override path gated by RBAC + feature flag (per-tenant) without too much risk.
- We can require “justification” and an “approver” field, but if we want true 2-person approval in-product (request + approve), that’s more UI + workflow. Short-term, we can do “override requires elevated role AND must include approver name + ticket id”, with enforcement that approver != actor.
- We can restrict override by optimization type (quantization vs other) and by gate result type (timeout/unavailable vs fail).

Audit logging:
- We will log a single OptimizeConfigChange event that includes: proposed config delta, gate result summary, override flag, justification, ticket link, actor, approver, and correlation ids to the eval run.
- We can also emit a separate OptimizeGuardrailsOverride event if you want “explicit override” to be easy to query.

If the decision is “no override for fail”, that’s simplest and safest.

Ethan



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Optimize Guardrails gating override policy (Enterprise tiers)

I’m open to an enterprise-only override, but we need crisp controls.

Before I approve, answer these:
1) For which tiers exactly? (Dedicated + Private only? Any “hosted enterprise”?)
2) Do we allow override on a true FAIL (quality regression) or only on TIMEOUT / runner unavailable?
3) Who is allowed to execute the override? What is the approval model?
4) What’s the audit log payload, and what’s retained vs ephemeral? Customers will ask for this.

Also: I do not want a loophole that becomes the default path. There must be rate-limiting and visibility.

Priya



From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Optimize Guardrails gating override policy (Enterprise tiers)

Priya — proposed answers / recommendation below (based on customer asks + what we can defend in audits):

1) Tiers
- Only Dedicated and Private.
- Not for self-serve hosted API tiers.
- “Hosted Enterprise” (if we have it in pricing) should follow Dedicated rules only if it has an enterprise contract + named admins; otherwise no.

2) When override is allowed
- Default: override permitted ONLY for TIMEOUT / runner unavailable (i.e., we could not complete evaluation), not for “FAIL”.
- Exception: override on FAIL permitted only for non-quantization changes and only with explicit approval + follow-up rerun requirement.
- Quantization: no override on FAIL (ever). For TIMEOUT/unavailable, we can either (a) still block or (b) allow override with stricter approval. I recommend we keep quantization strict: block on timeout too, unless exec wants otherwise.

3) Who can override
- Restricted RBAC role (tenant-level): “Optimize Guardrails Admin” (named individuals).
- Require a second approver for any override that proceeds without a completed eval (i.e., timeout/unavailable). This can be captured as an approver field + ticket reference, even if the actual request/approval workflow is out-of-band initially.

4) Auditing / retention (what customers will ask for)
Must record (at minimum):
- who initiated the apply (actor id/email)
- when
- tenant + project/route identifiers
- what config changed (old/new)
- optimization type (quant/batching/caching/routing)
- guardrails policy version + thresholds version
- prompt-set revision(s) + eval suite id(s)
- gating outcome + failure reason (metric deltas and CI summary, or timeout/unavailable)
- override_used=true/false
- override_justification (free text)
- override_approver (identity)
- override_ticket_link (Jira/ServiceNow/etc)
- expiration/TTL for the override (e.g., valid for this single apply only)

Retention: audit events retained per normal audit log policy; eval artifacts can expire earlier (we can keep ids + summary fields in audit logs even if artifacts roll off).

If you’re OK with this direction, we’ll update PM-844 and give Ethan’s team a “must-have fields” list for the event spec.

Ava



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 12:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Optimize Guardrails gating override policy (Enterprise tiers)

Approved with the following policy (effective for pilot):

- Scope: Dedicated + Private only. No override for self-serve hosted.
- Quantization:
  - If gate FAILS: hard block, no override.
  - If TIMEOUT/unavailable: hard block for now (we can revisit after we see runner reliability + false positive/negative rates).
- Non-quantization changes (batching/caching/routing):
  - Gate FAIL: block by default. Override allowed only with (1) restricted RBAC role and (2) a second approver recorded, plus a linked ticket and justification.
  - Gate TIMEOUT/unavailable: override allowed with restricted RBAC + second approver recorded + ticket + justification.
- Rate limit: cap overrides per tenant per week (pick a conservative number; I’d rather force escalation than allow routine use).
- Auditability: all overrides must be clearly queryable/exportable. Keep minimal required fields in audit logs even if eval artifacts expire.

This is not a backdoor. We will review override volume weekly during pilot; if it spikes, we remove the capability.

Ava — please circulate a final one-pager summary for signoff + include in the customer-facing posture doc.

Priya



From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 16, 2025 at 4:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Optimize Guardrails gating override policy (Enterprise tiers)

Thanks — captured and will operationalize.

Action items:
- (Ava) Update PM-844 with the approved policy + rate limiting requirement.
- (Ethan) Ensure ENG-3920 enforces:
  - tier restrictions
  - quantization block rules (fail + timeout)
  - second approver != actor check (at least enforced as separate field)
  - required ticket link + justification
  - per-tenant weekly cap
- (Aditya) Align UX copy: make it explicit that override is a risk acceptance and will be audited; for quantization, message should say “Override not permitted for this optimization type.”
- (Ava/Ethan) Confirm audit event fields are present in OptimizeConfigChange and are exportable for enterprise requests.

I’ll send the one-pager summary in a separate email once PM-844 is updated.

Ava
